name: Fineotex Chemical Ltd
title: Fineotex Chemical Ltd - 533333 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Analyst / Investor Meet - Outcome

read.thesis: Consol revenue ~INR 387 cr (+165% YoY) on US CrudeChem consolidation; Texas plant only 63% utilised with 148k MTPA capacity, but management gave no numeric margin or volume guidance and relied on promotional answers.

summary.headline: Fineotex Q1 FY27 total income rose 165% YoY to INR 386.72 crore, with EBITDA of INR 59.14 crore at a 15.70% margin, driven by the US CrudeChem consolidation.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 consolidated total income was INR 386.72 crore against INR 146.62 crore a year earlier, mainly from a full quarter of the US operations (CrudeChem Technologies Group, CCTL). EBITDA rose 134.7% YoY to INR 59.14 crore, with margin at 15.70% versus 13.93% in the prior quarter, and PAT grew 92.67% to INR 48.21 crore. The Texas plant capacity was expanded to about 148,000 MTPA, with utilisation stated at about 63%. Management declined to give a fixed margin guidance, while reiterating USD 100 million (FY27) and USD 200 million (FY28) targets for the oil and gas segment.

segments.name: Oil and gas specialty chemicals (CCTL, US)
segments.commentary: Management said about 65% of revenue and about 55% of volume come from oil and gas, roughly INR 250 crore in the quarter. The Texas plant is now about 148,000 MTPA, and management said it is utilised at about 63%.

segments.name: Textile specialty chemicals (India, standalone business)
segments.commentary: Management said the base business is about INR 132 crore after deducting CCTL from consolidated revenue, against INR 137 crore in Q1 FY26, a 1-2% dip that it attributed to monsoon seasonality and competition. Management said pricing was passed on and that the textile business is flattish.

guidance_outlook: Oil and gas segment targets of USD 100 million in FY27 and USD 200 million in FY28, which management said are driven by order book and customer expectations rather than crude prices. Management said it expects the target to be reached by December 2028.
Management said it expects the Texas plant to be fully utilised within the coming few quarters, with scope to add a second shift.
Management said it has no fixed consolidated EBITDA margin guidance. It reiterated the aspiration of 18% margin but did not commit to it.
Management said margins are sustainable, with pass-through of raw material and freight costs through war surcharges in the US.
capex_capacity: Texas manufacturing capacity was expanded to about 148,000 MTPA (from about 80,000 MTPA), taking group capacity to about 268,000 MTPA, per an analyst's figure that management did not dispute.
Texas utilisation is about 63%, with management saying another 30-40% could be added on the existing plant.
Management said further capex needed to support growth is about USD 1-2 million, which it does not regard as material.
A second shift is available on the Texas plant, and new high-performance machinery was installed in the expansion.
The new Indian plant at FSPL Specialties, commissioned in August 2025, operates under Section 115BAB at a 15% tax rate.
demand_pricing: Management said it passes on raw material and freight cost increases through a US war surcharge, and that margins are sustainable even if prices fall.
Management said the order book for CCTL is not a fixed tender-based order book. It said demand is perennial once wells are producing, with short weather-related interruptions.
Management said it has started selling to Canada and has won a Saudi business order. It also said a customer has an USD 8 billion Aramco order where Fineotex's specialty package is used.
Management said textile demand is supported by Indian export recovery, with UK, EU and US trade deals improving sentiment.
Management said it competes with US specialty chemical majors on price, and that its performance is equivalent.

qa_highlights.question: What is the top-line and bottom-line growth outlook from the Texas capacity addition, and are there any inorganic targets?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Texas is at about 63% utilisation, with room to add 30-40%. It said it is evaluating acquisitions with a focus on synergy and value, and will disclose to exchanges once an advanced stage is reached.

qa_highlights.question: Is the USD 200 million FY28 oil and gas target dependent on crude prices?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the target depends on order book and customer relationships, not crude price. It said activity continues even at USD 60, and that crude is currently around USD 90-100.

qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone revenue and EBITDA decline YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the standalone figures exclude FSPL Specialties, the new Indian plant. Combined with FSPL, the dip is not visible, and the difference is an accounting presentation matter.

qa_highlights.question: What is CCTL's ROCE and does it need more capital?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said oil and gas is not capex-intensive and ROCE is among the best in the industry. Growth needs about USD 1-2 million of capex, and the business runs on one shift today.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 15.7% margin sustainable, and can the business reach the 18% level?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not guide to a fixed blended margin and that the blended margin is in the 13-14% range or better for CCTL. It said it aspires to better margins.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the CCTL forex gain or loss not clear?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FX gains or losses are reported separately as a foreign exchange item, not as other income, and that natural hedging exists through USD raw material purchases. It said the impact is small, around INR 1-2 crore.

risks_watch: Reported consolidated numbers depend heavily on CCTL, which is about 65% of revenue, so the base textile business is less visible.
The 63% Texas utilisation needs to rise to deliver the USD 100 million FY27 and USD 200 million FY28 oil and gas targets.
Management declined to give fixed margin guidance and did not explain the 18% aspiration in quantified terms.
Non-controlling interest (about 47% of CCTL) and the accounting for it were not clearly quantified on the call.
Textile base business was flat YoY; a rebound is expected in later quarters, but management has not given numbers.
Geopolitical volatility and freight and raw material price movements, with management saying pricing changes are unpredictable.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on the US oil and gas business and its growth targets. Evasive on specific margin and CCTL-level profitability questions, deferring to consolidated metrics and offline follow-ups.
key_quotes: So, it's not product selling, it's at least a combination of five, six product lines and we are competing and with the USA top specialty chemical companies and because of we being more leaner, we have an edge on pricing and the performance is equivalent.
So, we still have two years to that. I think it should not be a challenge going forward.
USD 1 million or USD 2 million investment here and there is not going to change the world for Fineotex at all at the moment.

financial_highlights.change: vs about 33% last year and about 29-30% last quarter

adds.what: Texas plant expansion to about 148,000 MTPA (from about 80,000 MTPA), already expanded
Second shift available on Texas plant (utilisation headroom of 30-40% on existing plant)

growth.why: Management reiterated USD 100m FY27 and USD 200m FY28 oil and gas targets, backed by CCTL order book and an Aramco-linked order, plus Texas capacity at about 148,000 MTPA with 63% utilisation and a second shift available; no fixed margin guidance given. Quarterly growth is largely from the US consolidation, while the standalone textile base dipped 1-2%.
